title: Validate and restore PostgreSQL logical backup after confirmed data loss
trigger: Customer-visible PostgreSQL data is missing or corrupted while the database process may still be reachable.
preconditions: confirm actual business-data loss independently of service health checks
capture affected and unaffected table counts plus the current schema contract
identify the backup recovery point and retain its checksum/catalog metadata
restore the backup into an isolated validation target before using it for destructive primary recovery whenever time and incident policy permit
compare validation-restore schema and business-data invariants with the approved recovery expectation
quiesce application writes before replacing the primary database
diagnostic_steps: compare /health/ready with customer-visible data counts or fingerprints
verify PostgreSQL reachability with pg_isready and a minimal query
run db/schema-contract.sql to determine whether schema is intact
inventory affected and unaffected business tables
inspect the pg_restore catalog for required schema/table data
verify the backup checksum against the retained checksum record
perform a clean validation restore and compare ticket count, ticket fingerprint, activity count, and schema contract before selecting that backup for recovery
mitigation_steps: stop or quiesce application writes before database replacement
terminate only sessions connected to the isolated recovery database when required
recreate the damaged logical database and restore from the previously validated custom-format backup
do not treat pg_restore exit status alone as recovery proof
do not overwrite a primary database from an untested backup when an isolated restore validation can be performed
do not claim this logical restore procedure covers PITR, physical backups, replication failover, or cross-region disaster recovery
validation_steps: schema-contract.sql passes on the restored primary
ticket row count matches the approved baseline/recovery point
deterministic ticket fingerprint matches the approved baseline/recovery point
customer_activity count matches the approved baseline/recovery point
a transactional write/rollback probe succeeds without changing the restored fingerprint
PostgreSQL readiness is healthy after recovery
retain backup checksum, restore catalog, validation-restore evidence, loss evidence, restore timings, and final integrity evidence
escalation_boundary: Escalate to DBA/platform/incident command when no validated backup exists, the required recovery point is ambiguous, writes cannot be safely quiesced, backup checksum/catalog validation fails, clean restore integrity does not match expectations, point-in-time recovery is required, replication/standby state must be coordinated, physical corruption is suspected, or recovery would overwrite data that may need forensic preservation.
